edits.find:
# Bugbot triage

Use this reference when the Babysit playbook (`../playbooks/babysit.md`) handles Bugbot or review-automation comments. The goal is not to ignore Bugbot by default.
edits.replace:
# Review-bot triage

Use this reference when the Babysit playbook (`../playbooks/babysit.md`) handles review-bot comments. On GitHub they are ordinary review threads from accounts such as `cursor[bot]` (Bugbot), `claude[bot]`, CodeRabbit, or Copilot. The goal is not to ignore a bot by default.
edits.why: A Claude Code user gets review comments from several bots, not only Cursor's Bugbot. The skeptical triage applies to every one of them.

edits.find: Watch each PR with PR and CI event subscriptions when your harness has them.
edits.replace: Each worker's completion notification wakes you, and `gh pr view` and `gh pr checks` give a PR's live state when you act on it.
edits.why: Claude Code ships no PR or CI event subscription. Channels, a research preview, deliver a CI webhook only through a channel server the user builds. /autofix-pr hands the PR to a cloud session that pushes its own fixes, a second writer on the owner's branch, and the Monitor tool watches by running a script that usually polls, which this playbook forbids. A background subagent notifies its parent when it finishes, so that notification is the event, and gh reads the live state. Checked against code.claude.com/docs/en/commands and tools-reference on 2026-10-29.

edits.find: Call no scripts, run no polling loops, and never relay messages or status between agents.
edits.replace: Call no scripts, run no polling loops, and never relay messages or status between agents. When the session compacts, re-read poteto-mode's `SKILL.md` and this playbook before your next step, because compaction keeps only part of them.
edits.why: A multi-day coordinator compacts, and compaction re-attaches only the start of each loaded skill, which cuts poteto-mode short and drops this playbook.

edits.find: Run workers on a new cloud VM (`environment: "cloud"`) unless the work needs this machine: a `control-ui` or `control-cli` runtime check (from `cursor-team-kit`), local transcripts, a simulator, or auth that exists only here.
edits.replace: Run each worker with `isolation: "worktree"`, and name the branch or commit to check out in its kickoff. Every worker runs on this machine, so one that needs a `control-ui` or `control-cli` runtime check, local transcripts, a simulator, or auth that exists only here runs the same way. Workers share this machine's CPU, memory, and ports, so give each one that boots a surface its own ports and data directory.
edits.why: Claude Code's docs give subagents only `isolation: "worktree"`, and the Agent tool's `remote` value is gated and undocumented. So a worktree subagent on this machine stands in for a cloud VM, and the mapping's environment row has its brief name the branch or commit. It runs on this machine, so the exception for work that needs this machine is gone, and workers that share one machine collide on ports and data unless each gets its own. omc-pstack-fy bundles control-ui and control-cli.

edits.find: - **Fork when new work needs a worker's built state,** such as its checkout, uncommitted changes, or a running process. Message a worker only for a follow-up on the same work.
edits.replace: - **Continue a worker with `SendMessage` to its id only when new work needs its built state,** such as its checkout, uncommitted changes, or a running process, or when the work is a follow-up on its own task.
edits.why: Claude Code's fork, `subagent_type: "fork"`, copies the caller's context, not another agent's. SendMessage to a worker's id is the only way to reuse its state, so both cases go through it, as poteto-mode's Subagents section already says for checkouts, uncommitted changes, and running processes.

edits.why: A Claude Code coordinator sees a sub-coordinator's spawns only in that agent's transcript, and this playbook forbids messaging an agent to check on it. Nested subagent transcripts sit in the session's subagents/ folder beside their parent's (observed on 2026-10-29).

edits.find: 5. **Spawn one blinded judge** on a different model family per the **arena** skill's Phase C.
edits.replace: 5. **Spawn one blinded judge** as the **arena** skill's Phase C does, but take its model from the `second opinion` line. edits.find:
# Transcripts dir: ~/.cursor/projects/<slugified-repo-path>/agent-transcripts.
slug=$(printf '%s' "$main_wt" | sed 's#^/##; s#/#-#g')
transcripts="$HOME/.cursor/projects/$slug/agent-transcripts"
edits.replace:
# Claude Code keeps transcripts in ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/, where the slug is
# the workspace path with every character that is not a letter or digit
# changed to -. The search is recursive, so it also reads
# <session>/subagents/, where worktree subagents log.
slug() { printf '%s' "$1" | sed 's/[^A-Za-z0-9]/-/g'; }
transcripts="$HOME/.claude/projects/$(slug "$main_wt")"
# Claude Code hands rg to its own shell as a function, which a script does not
# inherit, so fall back to grep.
if command -v rg >/dev/null 2>&1; then search="rg -l"; else search="grep -rl"; fi
edits.why: Claude Code stores transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/ with its own slug rule, and its bundled rg is not on a script's PATH.
